report.text:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, single frontal view

ACCESSION: CXR-83741

HISTORY:
Postoperative evaluation.

COMPARISON:
None available.

FINDINGS:
Single frontal chest radiograph obtained. Postsurgical changes of the right hemithorax with multiple right-sided thoracostomy tubes in place. Right internal jugular central venous catheter tip projects over the lower SVC. Low lung volume exam.

Small right apical pneumothorax. Mild right basilar and perihilar patchy airspace opacity, favored postoperative subsegmental atelectatic change. Mild linear left basilar atelectatic opacity. No pleural effusion. Cardiomediastinal silhouette is not enlarged.

IMPRESSION:
1. Postsurgical changes of the right hemithorax with multiple right chest tubes in place.
2. Small right apical pneumothorax.
3. Mild bibasilar, right greater than left, postoperative atelectatic airspace opacities.
4. Right IJ central venous catheter tip projects over the lower SVC.

findings.label: Small right apical pneumothorax
findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is a small amount of air trapped in the upper part of your right lung, which can sometimes cause mild shortness of breath or chest pain.

findings.label: Right basilar and perihilar atelectasis
findings.raw_text: Mild right basilar and perihilar patchy airspace opacity, favored postoperative subsegmental atelectatic change.
findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is mild collapse of small air sacs in the lower part of your right lung, likely due to recent surgery.

findings.label: Left basilar atelectasis
findings.raw_text: Mild linear left basilar atelectatic opacity.
findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is mild collapse of air sacs in the lower part of your left lung, which is common after surgery.

findings.label: Right internal jugular central venous catheter
findings.raw_text: Right internal jugular central venous catheter tip projects over the lower SVC.
findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: A tube inserted into a vein in your right neck is correctly positioned with its tip near the heart.

negativeFindings.label: No pleural effusion
negativeFindings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is no excess fluid buildup around your lungs.

summary: The chest X-ray shows post-surgical changes in the right chest with chest tubes in place. There is a small amount of air (pneumothorax) in the right upper lung, along with mild collapse of air sacs (atelectasis) in both lower lungs. A central venous catheter is correctly positioned.
explanation: You have a small pocket of air in your right lung and some mild lung collapse, which are common after surgery. Your heart size is normal, and there is no fluid buildup around the lungs. The medical tubes are in the correct positions.
